summary: POC scoping workshop to decide hosting mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC) for Solstice MedTech's patient-facing summarization and triage assistant. Key constraints: PHI handling, data residency for EU clients, and strict auditability. Agreed success metrics (latency, throughput, and quality). Plan: 6-week pilot with 48-hour benchmark runs followed by a 2-week soak before acceptance.
topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; timeline and pilot acceptance; networking and compliance requirements; cost tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Evan Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Dr. Aisha Rahman (Solstice CTO), Tom Hsu (Infra Lead), Rachel Moore (Head of MLOps), Devon Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on hosting options and concrete benchmark/run plan. Customer emphasized PHI compliance and audit logs; exploring Dedicated vs Private for predictable latency vs Hosted for speed-to-market.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros and then jump into the hosting tradeoffs. Evan you'll take the tech on this one?
[00:08] Evan Chen: Yep, I'll cover the benchmark plan and what we need from you. Hi Aisha, Tom, Rachel, Devon.
[00:13] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Thanks. We're trying to lock down whether we go straight to Private or start with Hosted and move. Key is PHI, audit, and a predictable SLA for triage.
[00:25] Tom Hsu: Also to add, our traffic profile is spiky—peak outpatient hours 11am-2pm and evening 7pm-10pm. Concurrency might jump to ~90 concurrent sessions for the triage flow on weekdays.
[00:40] Rachel Moore: From MLOps side we use a batched inference pipeline today but this will be real-time, low latency, and per-request context windows of 600-1,200 tokens typically.
[00:53] Jamie Park: Great, that gives us sizing. Quick framing: Hosted gives fastest setup and cost-ease but has shared tenancy constraints; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable p95 latencies; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control for PHI and audit but adds lead time and ops overhead.
[01:10] Devon Patel: For security we need KMS integration and per-request audit logs retained for 7 years for some EU contracts — and SSO via SAML. 
[01:20] Evan Chen: Totally. We support KMS/HSM integrations, SSO, and audit logs. I will note though sometimes Fireflies transcriptions call it 'Sam El' sorry but SAML— yeah we support that. For the benchmark plan we propose a two-phase run: stage 1 is a 48-hour throughput + latency sweep for Hosted and Dedicated variants; stage 2 is a 2-week soak on the selected mode with real traffic replay.
[01:42] Dr. Aisha Rahman: What are your baseline acceptance numbers? We need specific SLOs to sign off.
[01:48] Jamie Park: Good call. Proposed success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for typical user prompt (<=1k tokens) on Dedicated; 2) End-to-end 99th percentile error rate < 0.1%; 3) Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with 2x burst headroom; 4) Quality: identical or better intent/summary F1 compared to current rule-based system (we'll run A/B evals on a 500-sample test set).
[02:20] Tom Hsu: 250ms p95 seems aggressive for 1k tokens. Is that including network RTT to our VPC?
[02:28] Evan Chen: That's infra-to-infra. For Hosted you'll see slightly higher p95 due to routing and multi-tenant variance, maybe 300-400ms in practice for same model. Dedicated typically hits the 200-250ms range if sequence length and batch behavior fit.
[02:40] Rachel Moore: Can you share the model variants you recommend? Quantized, fp16s? We care about hallucination rates for summaries.
[02:48] Evan Chen: We'll propose two model variants: a medium-sized open model with 8-bit quant (fastest, lower cost) and a higher-accuracy 16-bit variant. We'll include reranker for hallucinations. Also adaptive KV cache will help for conversational flows. FYI sometimes the transcription picks it up as 'K-V cash' in the transcript.
[03:05] Jamie Park: On cost tradeoffs: Hosted is easiest but variable cost; Dedicated gives better per-token economics at committed capacity; Private adds infra cost and ops but meets strict compliance. For this pilot we commonly recommend starting hosted for integration + benching, then move to Dedicated if burn and latency justify it — unless compliance forces Private.
[03:25] Devon Patel: Our legal team is leaning Private because of the EU PHI routing rules. But they are open to a Hosted pilot if data never leaves our VPC and you provide SOC2 plus audit exports. Is there a hybrid path?
[03:36] Evan Chen: Yes — we support a Private control plane + customer-managed compute where traffic passes through your VPC and logs are retained in your cloud — sort of a hybrid onramp. It reduces lead time vs full on-prem but keeps audit control.
[03:49] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Timeline? We have a regulatory window and would like production by end of Q2. How long for pilot then cutover?
[03:57] Jamie Park: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week): align on prompts and telemetry and sign off on benchmark plan. Week 1: Redwood runs 48-hour Hosted + Dedicated benchmarks (using your sample prompts) and shares results. Week 2-3: integration and any minor infra changes, choose mode. Week 4-7: 2-week soak + acceptance tests and security review. That puts a production decision within 6 weeks, and full cutover to Private (if chosen) might add 4-6 weeks for networking and certs. So end of Q2 is feasible.
[04:33] Tom Hsu: For the 48-hour benchmarks, what metrics and artifacts will you share? We need token-level cost, per-route latency, and error traces.
[04:41] Evan Chen: We'll deliver a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput graphs, CPU/GPU utlization, per-token cost estimates, and a sample of request/response traces (redacted). We'll also provide the scripts so you can re-run locally.
[04:56] Rachel Moore: What about regression detection on output quality? We need automatic alerts if new model rollout causes drop in F1.
[05:02] Maya Ortiz: Yes — Redwood Optimize ties model version to eval sets. For the pilot we'll set up a small eval harness with 500 test cases and run diff checks on quality. We'll include regression alarms based on F1 drop and human sampling.
[05:18] Devon Patel: On encryption, we need both data-at-rest KMS and in-transit TLS with mTLS for private peering.
[05:25] Evan Chen: Supported. We'll include KMS/HSM notes in the security pack. Also note: for Private on-prem installs we can integrate with your HSM but that adds orchestration steps.
[05:34] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Are there hard limits around request size or total context length? Some of our notes can be longer than 2k tokens.
[05:41] Evan Chen: Our runtime supports long context but you'll see higher latency. For >2k tokens we recommend forced truncation or summarization pre-step. We'll show latency curves in the benchmark.
[05:52] Jamie Park: Ok let's recap and concrete next steps. Action items — Jamie will share the security pack and network diagram; Evan will produce the benchmark script and run plan; Rachel to send sample prompts; Tom to send concurrency windows; Devon to share regulatory constraints. We'll schedule the benchmark run for this Friday once we have the prompts.
[06:12] Dr. Aisha Rahman: That works. One more ask — can you simulate token-level billing in the benchmark so procurement can estimate cost for committed Dedicated?
[06:20] Evan Chen: Yes we'll include a cost model with assumptions for tokens, batching, and expected hit rates for KV cache. We'll give both hosted per-token price and Dedicated amortized cost per token with commit assumptions.
[06:30] Jamie Park: Great. I'll send out meeting notes and invite for the deep dive on networking. Anything else?
[06:36] Rachel Moore: No, that's it from me. Thanks all.
[06:39] Tom Hsu: Thanks.
[06:41] meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: automatic captions occasionally mislabel acronyms (SAML -> Sam El), "KV cache" as "K-V cash", and Redwood product names sometimes misspelled. Natural speech disfluencies retained.
notes: Customer strongly leaning Private for compliance but open to Hosted pilot; explicit success criteria agreed; 6-week pilot plan with 48-hour benchmark. Benchmarks will include p95 latency, throughput, cost, and quality evals.
